answer.headline: CY 2024 home-CBSA per-capita income and passenger seat factor have a positive calculated association across South Atlantic commercial-service airports, and the rank interval includes no association
answer.body:
Across commercial-service airports in the Census South Atlantic division, the calculated Pearson correlation of home-CBSA per-capita income with passenger seat factor is {F126}. The calculated Spearman rank correlation is {F127}. The paired sample is {F130}.

The calculated Spearman bootstrap interval runs from {F128} to {F129}. The lower end is negative and the upper end is positive, so the interval includes no rank association.

Income is a calculated series: {F1.definition}, window {F1.period}. Passenger seat factor is a calculated series: {F63.definition}, window {F63.period}. Those wording placeholders point at the ABY input rows {F1.label} and {F63.label}. They are not a division total.

claims.text: The Pearson correlation of CY 2024 home-CBSA per-capita income with passenger seat factor is {F126}, calculated. The Spearman rank correlation is {F127}, calculated. The paired sample is {F130}.
The Spearman bootstrap interval is {F128} to {F129}, calculated.
Income in this correlation is {F1.definition} over {F1.period}, calculated. Passenger seat factor is {F63.definition} over {F63.period}, calculated.

A reliable association is not established. The Spearman interval includes a negative value and a positive value, so it is consistent with no rank association and with a positive association. The positive point estimates alone do not show that higher-income metros have higher seat factors.

assumptions: South Atlantic means the Census South Atlantic division. The place name resolves to that division exactly.

Commercial service means airports in that division at or above the resolver commercial-service enplanement floor. Airports below that floor are excluded, including smaller commercial-service airports.

Income and seat factor are both taken on CY 2024, the latest year with home-CBSA income and a complete calendar year of seat factor. Later seat-factor months are left out because income coverage ends in CY 2024.
Each airport is one observation. Airports that share a home CBSA are kept separate.
limitations: This is an association across airports. It does not hold size, hub status, or carrier mix fixed, and it is not a cause, a valuation, or a screening rank.
Home-CBSA income is an administrative proxy for the market area, not a measured catchment. Airports in one metro repeat one income value, so the points are not independent metros.
RBN is in the screened set and absent from the paired sample. An exploratory airport-to-CBSA crosswalk returns no home-CBSA title for RBN. That crosswalk result is exploratory, not a catalog metric.
Passenger seat factor does not measure unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, or profitability.
The rank interval still contains a positive association, so the data also do not establish that income and seat factor are unrelated.
